chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu al-Jahm from Fudayl al-A'war said:

I witnessed Mu'adh ibn Kathir saying: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have become wealthy, so I will leave trade.' He said, 'If you do so, your intellect will decrease, or something similar.'

key_terms.أَوْ نَحْوَهُ: or something similar / or the like

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam advise against leaving trade after becoming wealthy?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Mu'adh ibn Kathir against retiring from trade upon achieving wealth, linking commercial activity to the preservation of intellect ('aql). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the dignity of labor and the idea that active engagement in one's profession prevents mental stagnation and maintains spiritual vigilance. The narration underscores that trade is not merely an economic necessity but a means of sustaining intellectual and moral acuity.
